title: No document tells an operator how to set a campaign up well
foundBy: user report (host): "we haven't really told the user of cs-campaign about best practices for how to setup campaigns"
details:
Nothing tells an operator how to set a campaign up well.

The documents each have a job, and none of them is judgement. README is the tour. INSTALL is setup. MANUAL is every command, flag, file, variable, exit code and diagnostic. PROTOCOL states the protocol, SPEC states what the behaviour must be, and AGENTS routes while holding no knowledge of its own.

MANUAL comes closest, with a five step shape and an authoring section, and both are mechanics: where the files go, what the orientation already says. Neither answers how to scope a mission, how many members to give it, how to phase the work, or what a good brief contains.

SAC-006 is the evidence. Role briefs were failing campaigns because their authors could not see the orientation, and the fix made that text readable. What still has no home is the other half: what to write once you can see it.

A command would carry it the way `manual` carries the manual, so an operator with the binary and no clone can read it. The name `authoring` is free, and AUTHORING.md does not exist.

This is an editorial decision about a document set whose jobs were assigned deliberately, so the shape belongs to the maintainer rather than to whoever files this.

notes.text: The scope may be wider than authoring. Running a campaign asks for judgement too. When to leave a stalled orchestrator alone, what to read in observe's two panes, and when a finding is worth more than a fix. MANUAL's Notes for agents carries several of those as bare rules with no reasoning attached. A document covering both halves would have a name like RUNNING.md rather than AUTHORING.md, and the command would follow it. The name is worth settling before the outline.

The document and its command are landed in 12ef20f. `cs-campaign playbook` prints PLAYBOOK.md from inside the binary, the way `manual` prints MANUAL.md. The scope is the whole lifecycle, settled with the user: designing a team, writing the mission and the briefs, running and monitoring, harvesting and closing out. The name PLAYBOOK was chosen over RUNNING because AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md already use running a campaign for driving the harness at all. MANUAL keeps every imperative and gains a pointer, and the reasoning moved across. The text is a first draft read out of SPEC and MANUAL, and it awaits the user's review and the learnings from earlier campaigns.
